title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2610.23845v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. translated_title: 科学发现中AI驱动的可复现性与分析稳健性
translated_abstract: 可复现且分析稳健的研究结果对科学进步至关重要，但评估这些特性通常需要昂贵的人工投入。我们研究了大语言模型（LLM）智能体能否帮助自动化复现和稳健性分析，并以监测、流行病学和最终结果（SEER）数据库为基础开展了医学案例研究——SEER是一个被广泛使用的美国癌症登记数据库，是数万篇已发表研究的数据来源。首先，我们推出了SEER-Repro，这是一个包含20篇已发表的基于SEER的论文及其研究结果复现所需数据和资源的基准。其次，我们创建了一个AI智能体，成功复现了2,190个原子声明中的77.4%，同时为进一步分析提供了可执行的基线。第三，我们开发了一个智能体分析流水线，通过识别每个医学发现背后的分析选择、提出可辩护的替代方案并重新运行分析，来测试医学发现的稳健性。
tldr: 该研究推出SEER-Repro基准并开发AI智能体，成功复现了77.4%的基于SEER数据库的医学研究声明，同时通过智能体分析流水线自动化测试医学发现的分析稳健性。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the SEER-Repro benchmark and an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 claims from SEER-based medical studies, along with an agentic analysis pipeline to automatically test the analytical robustness of medical findings.
